statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring, f:X→Y and f′:X′→Y′ arbitrary scheme morphisms, v:X′→X and b:Y′→Y with a Cartesian square, c a compactification of f, and t,t′ proper/open/proper presentations with supplied Cartesian representatives of all three factors. Put E_t=openNormalization(c);B(c,t). Let c′=c.ofIsPullback(sq), and chi be the successive proper/open/proper exchange from [def-pur-etale-graph-presentation-maps]. Then (E_t whiskered by b*) ; chi_t = chi_ofCompactification(c) ; (v* whiskered by E_t′). The source Cartesian representative is the explicit ofCompactificationBaseChange(c,sq).

proof.text: For each word of proper direct images and open extensions, retain its top and bottom functors and its successive base-change exchange. An isomorphism of such words is compatible when whiskering its top comparison with pullback and then exchanging equals exchanging and then whiskering its bottom comparison. Naturality proves closure under horizontal composition, and cancellation of the endpoint isomorphisms proves closure under inverses. Functor associators and unitors satisfy compatibility directly. The proper and inverse-open compositor compatibilities are exactly the two composition clauses of sfExactExchangePasting. For the open identity comparison, use the identity base-change equation of the unbounded formalism; adjunction conjugacy identifies its normalization with the actual descended open identity isomorphism.

proof.text: Construct the maps between T=P×Y C and T′, between both open graph neighborhoods, and between their intersection by pullback.map. Prove that the projection squares are Cartesian directly from the pullback universal property: one Cartesian input square suffices for the corresponding opposite projection. Check equality of the graph maps after composing with both projections. Cancellation of Cartesian rectangles then shows that the squares over s1, s2, and s12 are Cartesian. The existing explicit graph-model theorem supplies only properness witnesses for these fixed graph maps.

proof.text: Apply the proper/open cube and its Cartesian normalization to the two side squares. Combining each interchange with the proper compositor gives compatible side comparisons. Apply the same cube to the two identity-top graph triangles; combine these with the open identity comparison to obtain the graph-triangle isomorphisms used by B12. On the intersection, invert the first triangle comparison, compose the two open maps, transport along pullback.condition, split the other two open maps, and apply the second triangle comparison. Whisker by the common proper direct image, paste the first side, this middle comparison, and the inverse second side. The resulting top and bottom isomorphisms are exactly openNormalization followed by the specified graph comparison: the inserted derived direct-image identity and its inverse cancel. The boundary exchanges reduce definitionally to the two specified presentation exchanges. Their compatibility is the claimed equality.

theorem etaleGraphFromOpen_baseChange
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    (c : Compactification f) (v : X' ⟶ X) (b : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (sq : IsPullback v f' f b)
    (t : EtaleGraphPresentation f) (t' : EtaleGraphPresentation f')
    (dt : t.BaseChange t' v b) :
    Functor.whiskerRight
        (etaleGraphOpenNormalization A c ≪≫ etaleGraphComparisonFromOpen A c t).hom
        D((b)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]) ≫ etaleGraphPresentationExchange A dt =
      etaleGraphPresentationExchange A
          (EtaleGraphPresentation.ofCompactificationBaseChange c sq) ≫
        Functor.whiskerLeft D((v)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A])
          (etaleGraphOpenNormalization A (c.ofIsPullback sq) ≪≫
            etaleGraphComparisonFromOpen A (c.ofIsPullback sq) t').hom
